text.p: Uraco Holdings Ltd is monitoring developments at CAM International Holdings Ltd, where two directors have been accused of fraud, Uraco group financial controller Philip Tan said on Tuesday.
"At the moment, we are sitting tight and we are waiting to see what is going to happen. We are reviewing the situation," Tan told Reuters.
Uraco bought a 6.3 percent stake in CAM in early 1996. Tan said Uraco paid S$1.00 for each CAM share and the total investment amounted to S$15.5 million.
He said the stake was a long term investment and would not have an impact on the Uraco's financial bottom line this year.
CAM shares were last traded at S$0.625 each prior to their suspension on April 29.
Uraco share prices have been under selling pressure since news broke of possible fraud at CAM. They touched a new 1997 low of S$0.84 in early trading this morning.
"It is too early to say what the impact will be. But we are not making any provisions," said Tan.
He said Uraco had not spoken to CAM officials since news broke over the weekend of an auditors report ON CAM to the Finance Ministry.

The report, by auditors Ernst & Young, was made public by the Stock Exchange of Singapore (SES) on Monday night. It said it believed certain transactions by two directors amounted to criminal breaches of trust.
The SES has asked CAM to respond to the report.
CAM officials were not immediately available for comment.
